objections.claim: The command flow's step 2 defines positionals as "args not starting with `--`" and exits 2 on any count ≠ 1. `--root` takes a value (`CONFIG_SPEC: "--root": { arity: 1 }`), so `faff config unset models --root /tmp/repo` yields positionals `["models", "/tmp/repo"]` — count 2 → exit 2 with the usage message, every time. The flag is dead on arrival under the spec's own pseudocode.
objections.evidence: HOW → "Command flow" step 2 (`positionals = args not starting with "--"`; `IF count != 1 … return 2`) vs the CLI-surface table row `faff config unset <dotted.key> [--local] [--dry-run] [--root DIR]` and the doc-row DONE item, both of which advertise `--root`. The spec says `cmdConfigUnset` "mirrors `cmdConfigSet`'s order: argument checks…" — `cmdConfigSet` gets away with the same flag-value-blind filter only because it reads `positionals[0]`/`[1]` and silently ignores `[2]`; the "exactly one" rule removes that accident of tolerance.
objections.predicted_consequence: `faff config unset <key> --root DIR` always exits 2; the `docs/guide/cli.md` row and surface table advertise a flag that never works, and the `config set --root` test parity the spec's helper style implies cannot be written for `unset` without deviating from the normative pseudocode.
objections.disposition_rationale: cmdConfig strips --root and its value before any sub-verb runs (config.js cmdConfig), so cmdConfigUnset never sees it; one-line note added to step 2

objections.claim: The spec's only stated downstream consumer is FAFF-1198's migration, which will call `faff config unset models` (and `effort`) across adopter repos. On any repo where the key was never set — or where a prior migration pass already removed it — the verb exits 3. The spec never states whether exit 3 is a caller-tolerated "already gone" or a failure, and FAFF-1198's contract section (per the critique's deps note) specifies only the error message and the no-namespace-guard posture, not the exit-3 handling.
objections.evidence: Spec CLI-surface table ("Key absent | 3"), smoke-test step 6 (`faff config unset models -> exit 3`), and the critique's deps paragraph ("The other-file note … gives FAFF-1198's migration the stale-overlay signal it needs") — the migration flow is named as the reason this ticket exists, but the absent-key exit semantics for that flow are unspecified.
objections.predicted_consequence: FAFF-1198's migration prose must independently decide whether exit 3 aborts or continues; if it treats non-zero as failure, a partially-migrated fleet re-runs fail on already-clean repos. If it must tolerate exit 3, that tolerance is an undocumented cross-ticket contract discovered at build time.
objections.disposition_rationale: one-line clarification added to the spec

objections.claim: For a file with duplicate keys in one window, `unset` removes the first match, the reader keeps the last, the round-trip proof fails, and the verb exits 2 — forever. There is no path by which `unset` can ever succeed on that file, and the spec offers no remedy (the carve-out for hand-edits was explicitly not extended). The file is left byte-identical, so the operator is stuck in the exact position the CLI-only rule was meant to eliminate: only a hand-edit (forbidden) or a full `config init` rewrite can clear it.
objections.evidence: Spec edge-case table row "Duplicate keys in one window | First match is removed; the reader keeps the last, so the round-trip fails and nothing is written", plus the DONE item asserting this exits 2 with no write.
objections.predicted_consequence: not separately stated — duplicate top-level keys in a hand-authored `.faffrc.yaml` are rare, so this is a taste-level gap; but when it fires, the operator has no sanctioned remedy, which is the same class of dead end the ticket exists to remove.
